text:
kim: Heads-up — us-west-2 fleet is creeping into saturation, GPU util ~94% and queue backlog increasing. Thinking about switching from a single global FIFO to per-route logical queues + a global admission controller. Want to avoid both head-of-line blocking and wasted reserved capacity. Thoughts? :warning:

infra-bot: [AUTO] cluster-us-west-2 GPU utilization=94% p99_queue_ms=3200 dropped_requests=12 in last 15m

sasha: per-route queues make sense for fairness across customers. prevents one noisy long-running route from stalling others. but we need accurate per-route capacity accounting (tokens = expected tokens per request).

omar: tradeoff: many small per-route reservations fragments capacity. if we reserve too strictly small routes starve when capacity is tight. can we do dynamic shares instead of fixed partitions?

taylor: we ran priority queues in staging. critical routes improved latency, but long jobs in high-priority queue still caused head-of-line for other high-priority requests (no preemption). preemption + state cleanup was messy.

kim: proposal: hybrid approach — per-route logical queues + a global admission controller that issues "capacity tokens". Routes get soft-min shares; priority raises token multiplier but admission still respects global pool. Preemption only as last resort. Sketch config below:

kim: ```
admission:
  global_tokens: 1000        # tokens approximating concurrent-kernel capacity
  per_route_min: 5          # soft guaranteed tokens per active route
  priority_mult:
    gold: 2                  # gold requests consume 2x token budget (gives priority)
    silver: 1.2
    bronze: 1
  max_in_flight_per_gpu: 8  # backpressure per GPU
  reclaim_on_idle_secs: 30  # reclaim soft shares if unused
```

sasha: also need to split based on batching path: small low-latency requests should hit a fast-path (small max_batch, tight deadline) vs throughput path for big batches. admission should be aware of batch profiles.

omar: metrics we need: queued_requests_by_route, token_consumption_by_route, preemptions, backlog_seconds_p50/p95/p99, reclaimed_tokens. and an alert when global_token_util > 0.9 for >5m.

taylor: cost reminder: per-route reservations increase risk of idle GPUs (wasted cost). recommend starting with soft-shares + tenant-reclaim logic, avoid hard static partitions. Also add an emergency fallback: when critical SLOs are threatened, auto-fallback to a lower-cost model or a degraded path.

kim: agreed. next steps: POC in staging (us-west-2) with two routes: `api/chat` and `api/embeddings`. Run a 48h load test with mixed job sizes + priority classes. Need volunteers for harness, metrics, and controller.

sasha: I can stand up the load harness and generate mixed token jobs (small chat vs big embedding batches).

omar: I'll wire metrics and dashboards, plus the alert rules for token_util and backlog.

taylor: I'll start the admission-controller skeleton and the reclaim logic. won't enable preemption initially.

kim: awesome — sync tomorrow 10:00am to review POC plan and expected failure modes. Thanks all. :thumbsup:
